thread:
oncall-bot: Pager: Dedicated GPU pool 'eu-west-2-reserved' at 95% utilization, queue depth increasing (avg 430s wait). Autoscaler failing to add nodes (rate-limit error). Paging SRE oncall @Priya G.
Priya G: seeing a spike in queued requests and throttles for reserved tenants. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/pools/eu-west-2-reserved — CPU/GPU mem look saturated.
Marco L: autoscaler logs show repeated 429 from cloud control plane: 
```
ERROR autoscaler: scale request rejected: rateLimitExceeded: Too many requests
request_id=abc123 ts=2026-04-02T09:02:11Z
```
Priya G: confirmed. Also eviction loop kicked in for best-effort workloads but reserved tenants still stuck in queue.
Nadia S: what are impacted tenants? any enterprise reservations blocked?
Priya G: yes — tenant ids: T-8721 and T-9903 are seeing tail latency > 20s per token and many requests 429'd by our gateway. CS flagged T-8721 in the portal.
Eve C: I'm on the CS thread with T-8721 — they're seeing model calls timing out, some requests failing. They're asking for ETA and workaround.
Liang W: checking kernel-level GPU slots — looks like 100% on gpus 0-15 on a subset of nodes, but a few nodes have 0% (they were cordoned).
Marcus R: autoscaler is hitting our control-plane quota for creating new VM instances. The cloud account has a soft limit; our retry/backoff is linear and the cloud is rate limiting.
Marco L: I can flip the autoscaler to exponential backoff and increase jitter, but that won't instantly free capacity. Do we want to temporarily bump reserved->preemptible eviction threshold to free some GPUs?
Priya G: options I see: 1) Evict best-effort workloads from reserved pool (immediate but impacts non-reserved customers). 2) Manual scale up by infra (requires cloud quota bump or manual instance creation). 3) Re-route some reserved traffic to a compatible fallback pool in us-east (higher latency). 4) Ask CS to throttle the enterprise customers gracefully.
Eve C: T-8721 will accept a short degradation if we can provide deterministic headroom. They asked for degraded QPS rather than timeouts.
Nadia S: I can take on manual scaling. Marcus, can we request instance creation now with higher burst? Who owns the cloud quota ticket?
Marcus R: I opened a cloud support ticket earlier but it's low priority. I can escalate. Meanwhile I can create 4 extra instances under a different project (temp) but need 10-15 mins and a manual route update.
Priya G: let's do immediate mitigations in parallel. Marcus: manual instances + route update. Nadia: coordinate eviction of best-effort. Marco: adjust autoscaler backoff/jitter. Liang: start draining candidate nodes for controlled eviction of non-reserved batches. Eve: message T-8721 that we're actively mitigating, ETA ~15-25m, we will throttle gracefully to maintain throughput.
Marcus R: creating instances now (action). Running commands: 
```
# temp instance create (internal)
rw-cli cloud instances create --count 4 --flavor g5x --tag emergency-burst --region eu-west-2
```
Marco L: changing autoscaler backoff to exponential: 
```
PATCH /autoscaler/config
 {"backoff_base_ms":2000, "backoff_factor":2.5, "max_backoff_ms":60000 }
```
Priya G: eviction plan: move best-effort pods to preemptible pool and reduce their concurrency. Liang, post the evict command you used.
Liang W: using controlled evict: 
```
kubectl cordon node gpu-node-42 && kubectl drain node gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
```
Liang W: starting controlled eviction now. Moving ~120 jobs off reserved pool. Progress 20% -> 40% -> 70% in the last 6 minutes.
oncall-bot: Incident annotation: priority=high, impact=enterprise-tenants, incident_id=INC-20260402-43
Priya G: update: queue depth dropping from 430s avg wait to 120s. Some reserved requests still queued.
Eve C: T-8721 sees reduced error rate, but reports higher latency — they're okay if errors go down.
Marcus R: instances are up. Route update in progress. Running: 
```
rw-cli routes attach --pool eu-west-2-reserved --instances emergency-burst-*
```
Marco L: autoscaler backoff patched, we'll let it attempt slow retries rather than hammering API. Also enabled ephemeral throttle relief policy to allow one scale per 30s.
Nadia S: eviction completed on 6 nodes, reclaimed ~14 GPUs. Observability: token-level cost/latency shows reserved tail latency improving.
Priya G: queue depth now ~40s avg wait, throttles decreased by 80%. Good. Keep monitoring for 20m.
Eve C: sent update to customers: "We've opened emergency capacity and evicted non-critical workloads. You may see higher latency for a short period, but errors should be reduced. We'll continue to monitor and follow-up."
Liang W: one noisy tenant process was found hogging CUDA contexts on node gpu-node-37, we isolated container and restarted runtime. That freed 2 GPUs immediately.
Marco L: logging note — add alert for control-plane rateLimitExceeded to avoid autoscaler blind spot. Ticketed: AUTOSCALE-391.
Priya G: root cause hypothesis: sudden best-effort burst + noisy tenant with long-lived CUDA contexts + cloud API throttling prevented autoscaler from provisioning headroom. Postmortem to include: better control-plane backoff, per-tenant runtime isolation, and emergency burst playbook.
oncall-bot: Handing off to SRE secondary @Nadia S at 1872501265. Next oncall check in 30m.
Nadia S: taking handoff. Will draft timeline and mitigation notes for postmortem. Anyone with additional logs drop them here.
Priya G: thanks team. Closing pager for primary oncall.
Marco L: leaving runbook snippet — recommended quick mitigation steps: 
1) cordon+drain best-effort nodes
2) create emergency instances in separate project if control-plane throttled
3) temporarily lower preemption threshold for reserved pools
4) communicate with CS with deterministic ETA and QPS cap
5) file autoscaler backoff/alert improvements

Eve C: T-8721 confirmed they’re stable. I will follow up with post-incident notes to customers.
Nadia S: capturing timeline and actions. Will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow.
Priya G: thread close plan: monitor 30m, if stable, mark resolved and start postmortem.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260402-43 status: mitigated -> monitoring at 1872501298
